title: AT&T Expands D-Wave Partnership to Optimize Telecom Network Operations and Agentic AI - Quantum Computing Report
gist: AT&T signed a commercial agreement to expand its use of D-Wave's quantum annealing technology into its agentic AI-driven network operations, citing a pilot that cut a network optimization workload from one hour to under 15 seconds, while also exploring D-Wave's gate-model roadmap for future quantum-safe network security.

insights.claim: AT&T signed a commercial agreement with D-Wave Quantum Inc. to expand its use of quantum annealing technology across its network infrastructure operations, building on earlier pilot benchmarks.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Marks a move from pilot to commercial-scale deployment of quantum annealing at a major telecom, a concrete data point for enterprise quantum ROI beyond hype.
insights.quote: Telecommunications leader AT&T (NYSE: T) has signed a commercial agreement with D-Wave Quantum Inc. (NASDAQ: QBTS) to expand its use of quantum annealing technology across its network infrastructure operations.
insights.locator: AT&T Expands D-Wave Partnership to Optimize Telecom Network Operations and Agentic AI

insights.claim: In pilot benchmarks, D-Wave's quantum annealing hardware reduced a network optimization processing workload from one hour to under 15 seconds.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: A quantified ~240x speedup on a real operational workload is a concrete benchmark investors can use to gauge near-term quantum advantage claims in optimization use cases.
insights.quote: quantum annealing hardware reduced a network optimization processing workload from one hour down to under 15 seconds

insights.claim: AT&T plans to layer D-Wave's quantum annealing capabilities directly into its agentic AI operational workflows to handle combinatorial optimization bottlenecks that challenge classical compute clusters.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Frames quantum annealing as a complement to, not a replacement for, AI agents in enterprise infrastructure — a hybrid AI/quantum stack pattern worth tracking at other large telecoms.
insights.locator: Integrating Quantum Annealing into Agentic AI Workflows

insights.claim: AT&T's autonomous agentic AI systems handling outage detection, fault isolation, and incident mitigation reduced total customer downtime by 12 million hours in 2025.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Establishes the operational baseline AI agents already deliver at AT&T before quantum augmentation, useful for benchmarking incremental gains from the D-Wave integration.
insights.quote: In 2025 alone, these automated systems helped reduce total customer downtime by 12 million hours.
insights.locator: AT&T's network management architecture increasingly relies

insights.claim: AT&T is applying quantum annealing to outage detection and response, accelerating real-time re-routing and power distribution decisions during unexpected physical fiber cuts or weather disruptions.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Shows a concrete, latency-sensitive network operations task where quantum annealing is being targeted first, ahead of broader rollout.

insights.claim: Field technician dispatch scheduling and route planning across dense urban and rural service zones is a targeted quantum optimization use case for AT&T.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: A logistics-style optimization problem (routing) is a classic near-term fit for quantum annealing, indicating where AT&T expects fastest payback.

insights.claim: AT&T is using quantum optimization for dynamic bandwidth allocation across converged 5G and fiber networks as AI-driven data demand scales up.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Directly ties quantum-optimization infrastructure investment to growth in AI-driven network data demand, linking two capex trends investors are watching.

insights.claim: AT&T is exploring quantum annealing for network build planning, improving physical layout calculations and capital expenditure efficiency for infrastructure expansion.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: If proven out, quantum-optimized capex planning could materially affect how AT&T allocates infrastructure spend — an early-stage but capital-relevant application to monitor.

insights.claim: Beyond its current annealing deployment via D-Wave's Leap quantum cloud platform, AT&T is evaluating D-Wave's accelerated gate-model development pipeline for future network security and quantum communications infrastructure.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Signals AT&T is positioning for a multi-platform quantum strategy (annealing plus gate-model), worth tracking as an indicator of telecom quantum-security roadmaps.
insights.locator: Multi-Platform Strategy and Future Gate-Model Applications

insights.claim: Following D-Wave's acquisition of Quantum Circuits, Inc. (QCI) and its dual-rail superconducting architecture roadmap, AT&T's Chief Data Office is exploring how future fault-tolerant quantum systems could support quantum key distribution (QKD) protocols, network encryption, and quantum-resilient communications architectures.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: D-Wave's QCI acquisition is a leading indicator for telecom-grade quantum-safe security development; watch for AT&T pilots on QKD or quantum-resilient encryption as a follow-on signal.
insights.quote: Following D-Wave’s recent acquisition of Quantum Circuits, Inc. (QCI) and its dual-rail superconducting architecture roadmap, AT&T’s Chief Data Office is exploring how future fault-tolerant systems could support quantum key distribution (QKD) protocols, network encryption, and quantum-resilient communications architectures.
insights.locator: Multi-Platform Strategy and Future Gate-Model Applications
